install.hint: Atlassian documents a separate install page per platform (macOS, Linux, Windows); follow the one for yours from the docs page. Nothing is automated here: the documented macOS Homebrew route needs a tap added before the install, which j.connect cannot express, and Atlassian states that each acli version is supported for only 6 months after release, so keep it current. Coverage: the official reference lists the command groups jira, admin, rovodev and feedback only. Jira is covered. Confluence and Bitbucket are NOT covered by this transport: use the atlassian-cloud descriptor (remote MCP server) for them where it supports them. Not verified against a real account: the Linux and Windows install steps, which of Jira, Confluence and Bitbucket the Atlassian Cloud MCP server serves, and whether the commands below exit non-zero when you are not signed in. Atlassian Government Cloud is not supported by acli.

auth.instructions: Create an Atlassian API token in your Atlassian account yourself. Put the token, your Atlassian site (for example yoursite.atlassian.net) and your account email in the environment variables ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN, ATLASSIAN_SITE and ATLASSIAN_EMAIL yourself, in your own shell or secret store; the variable names are a j.connect convention, acli reads no environment variables for sign-in. Then run `acli jira auth login` yourself in a terminal, passing the site and email as its --site and --email flags and piping the token to its --token flag on standard input, as the docs page shows, and tell me when you are done. Do not paste the token into this chat or into a project file; j.connect never handles it. A successful check means acli can reach Jira with the stored login. Not verified against a real account: the exact flags and whether the check fails when signed out.
